content.value_statement: Jest projects often fail because tests, mocks, asynchronous behavior, and configuration are inconsistent. This skill provides focused patterns for dependable JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and Node.js testing.
actual_capabilities: Creates Jest unit, asynchronous, class, React component, and hook test structures.
Explains built-in matchers, custom matchers, snapshots, lifecycle hooks, and test organization.
Designs function, module, timer, and external dependency mocks.
Configures Jest environments, transforms, aliases, setup files, coverage thresholds, and CI options.
Uses React Testing Library queries, user events, async utilities, and provider wrappers.
Shows MSW handlers for successful responses, server failures, network failures, and request assertions.
limitations: Requires Jest 29 or newer for the documented modern APIs.
Does not execute tests or guarantee compatibility with project-specific dependencies.
Vitest guidance is limited to APIs that are compatible with Jest.
Does not assess overall test quality beyond Jest-specific implementation concerns.

use_cases.title: Test React interactions
use_cases.description: Create accessible component tests with provider wrappers, user events, loading states, and asynchronous assertions.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend engineers using React Testing Library

use_cases.title: Mock Node.js dependencies
use_cases.description: Build isolated service tests with module mocks, rejected promises, timers, and explicit success and error cases.

use_cases.title: Standardize Jest projects
use_cases.description: Review configuration, setup files, coverage thresholds, test discovery, cache settings, and continuous integration workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a unit test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Jest unit test for [function] in [file]. Cover the successful result, invalid input, and one boundary case.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an existing test
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [test file] and improve its Jest assertions, setup, cleanup, and async handling. Preserve current behavior and explain each change.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a project
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Jest for [project type]. Include environment, transforms, setup files, module aliases, coverage thresholds, and compatible package versions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a testing strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced Jest strategy for [workflow]. Use module mocks, fake timers, MSW handlers, custom matchers, and CI diagnostics where appropriate.

output_examples.input: Create tests for a React login form that submits asynchronously and displays an API error.
output_examples.output: A test plan covering accessible queries, realistic typing and clicking, the loading state, successful submission, and an MSW error response.

output_examples.input: Review a TypeScript Jest setup with slow tests and missing coverage enforcement.
output_examples.output: Configuration recommendations for transforms, setup files, worker limits, coverage thresholds, cache use, and commands for identifying open handles.

output_examples.input: Explain why a mocked module keeps its state between tests.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis covering mock clearing, module resetting, import order, per-test implementations, and cleanup responsibilities.

best_practices: Assert observable behavior and use accessible Testing Library queries before test identifiers.
Reset mocks, handlers, timers, and shared state after each test.
Test successful, failure, loading, and boundary behavior with deterministic dependencies.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on snapshots when focused behavior assertions are clearer.
Do not use real network services, real time, or shared mutable state in unit tests.
Do not hide unresolved promises or open handles by increasing timeouts.

faq.question: Which Jest versions are supported?
faq.answer: The documented patterns target Jest 29 or newer and modern companion package versions.

faq.question: Can this skill help with Vitest?
faq.answer: Yes, for compatible matchers, mocks, lifecycle hooks, and test structures. Vitest-specific configuration may require separate guidance.

faq.question: Does it support React Testing Library?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers accessible queries, user events, provider wrappers, hooks, loading states, and asynchronous utilities.

faq.question: Can it test API behavior without real requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates MSW handlers for successful responses, errors, request capture, and per-test overrides.

faq.question: Will it run or modify my project?
faq.answer: The guidance can propose changes. The included checker only reads local project configuration and reports findings.

faq.question: Does it measure test quality?
faq.answer: It focuses on Jest implementation and troubleshooting. Broader test quality analysis is outside its stated scope.
